schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: STAGE 2 OF THE CHART CHAIN, and a machine of its own since 2026-08-13. It answers ONE narrow question — what BOUNDS this request? — and emits the smallest typed artifact that fully determines what the next stage needs. Template-fills from stage 1's BERTHED packet, never the conversation. The floor surfaces each ref'd component's charter falsifier/gates/owner VERBATIM with its address — it reports text and never decides what applies; a paraphrased constraint is a constraint with laundered provenance. Three strata, cheapest first: FLOOR (deterministic, this module), TREE (this nexus's own corpus through cairn/tools/tree), CEILING (the skill's assembly). The exit artifact berths in instance-space and the deposit-back lands it as the tree's memory of this class of request. THE FLOOR AUTHORS, IT DOES NOT ONLY REPORT: ``floor_packet`` writes ``constraints`` — every ref'd component's falsifier, gates and owner, verbatim, each carrying the charter path and the field it came from — and ``unknowns``, which is every ref it could not ground and why. ``bounds`` is not a candidate and never will be: what is in and out of scope for a request is a judgement about intent, not a lookup. Provenance for the two authored fields is DERIVED at ``validate_constrain`` by re-running the floor over the packet's own ``intent_ref`` and comparing, so a field earns ``floor`` only when the floor's answer can be REPRODUCED. AND SINCE 2026-08-14 THE FLOOR ALSO REPORTS THE INSTRUMENTS THAT WILL REFUSE THIS BUILD. For every component the request grounds to, it DISCOVERS the proofs that judge that component — by composing the tester's own collector (``cairn.devices.tester.cli.discover``), so the house has one idea of what a proof is and not two — then RUNS each one through ``TesterDevice().run_proof`` and emits a constraint of kind ``check`` carrying the state it is in RIGHT NOW, with the proof's repo-relative path as its source. A red instrument also rides out as an unknown, because a bound that is already failing is not a bound this build can be judged against until someone says which it is. The packet carries a ``cost`` field holding this firing's own wall time, so the selection rule's bound is measured rather than carried in an operator's head. WHAT EARNS THE KIND: a verdict that came from an execution. A check reported without being run is the charter prose again one indirection further out, and a run that could not happen is reported ``unrunnable`` — never omitted, because a shrinking denominator makes the remaining greens look total. WHAT THE FLOOR STILL REFUSES TO DO: decide what APPLIES. It reports which instruments exist and what state they are in; whether a red one bounds this particular request is the ceiling's judgement, and the floor supplies the unknown rather than the answer. It also does not run an instrument from inside an instrument — ``CAIRN_CONSTRAIN_FLOOR_RUNNING`` is set across the subprocess boundary and inherited by the child, so a proof that calls this floor (this machine's own does, seventeen times) cannot fork without bound; depth is capped at one by physics rather than by an exclusion list someone maintains.
why: Akien, verbatim 2026-08-13: "orient is a machine. the other pre-build steps are each their own machine." A machine is tools plus the glue that holds them together, and that is exactly the shape here: cairn/tools/chain's grammar plus this stage's own question. THE LIVED SYMPTOM the whole chain answers is a build that starts before anyone settled what was being built — the web-server carrier miss, bounds-checking that never ran to completion. A stage that is its own machine can be fired, proved, and replaced alone; one that is a function in a 1,300-line module cannot. WHY THE RECORD AND NOT A COMPLAINT LIST (Akien, 2026-08-13): "passing such a thing without inspecting it means passing a mystery if something downstream fails … if every machine and even some more complex tools have their own inspector and gate, then each has documented and controllable quality validation … we can backtrack and see exactly where something went awry even if it's not something we're specifically looking for yet." A complaint list is empty both when every check passed and when no check ran, so the stage downstream is handed a mystery in exactly the case he named. The entries that PASSED are the ones nobody was looking for. "We might have to add more or better inspection questions, but that's fine. we learn as we go" — so the question list grows, and every addition is one more entry a reader sees whether it passed or failed.

feedback.why: THE LINK IS IN THIS MODULE'S OWN CODE: inspect_constrain opens on intent_ref (constrain.py:163) and _read_orient_berth refuses anything that is not an orient berth (constrain.py:77) — the field is named for the intent it carries, but the file it reads is stage 1's. This module's docstring says the same thing from the other side: 'stage 2's input is stage 1's validated file, never the conversation.' Akien's rule for the -2- edge, 2026-08-14, verbatim: "the purpose of an inspector/gate combination is to qa THE OUTPUT OF THE THING BEFORE IT THATS COMING IN AS ITS INPUT. IF IT FAILS, GENERALLY THAT FEEDBACK GOES BACK TO THE UPSTREAM CREATIVE ENTITY. In some cases it skips levels." REFINED BY HIM THE SAME DAY, and the refinement is what `to` MEANS: "really it shouldn't be 'number of steps' it should be 'to the feedback target' which is likely to be the previous step." So this field is not a hop count and never was — it names the TARGET. The previous step is the common case, not the definition, and a route that lands elsewhere is not a special case needing a count. So the thing before constrain is orient, and orient is where a failure at this door lands. WHAT THIS ROUTE SERVES SQUARELY: upstream_berth_is_readable and request_identity_rides_the_chain are findings ABOUT orient's packet — an unreadable berth or a request identity that stopped riding the chain is orient's to fix and nobody else's. The one-address shape cannot split a segment's findings by which side of its door they indict; see cairn/tools/feedback filed edge (e).

invoke: fired by the skill that runs the chain; the writer door is write_constrain; the inspector is inspect_constrain(packet) and returns the proof record without taking a verdict, so a caller can READ what this stage proved without provoking its refusal
entry: Carved out of the chart machine on 2026-08-13 under Akien's ruling — "chart is a skill, it calls a collection of machines. that's the intention." The chart charter it was carved from is the design record of the whole chain and now berths with the skill at cairn/skills/chart/intention+why.json; this file holds only what is THIS component's. THE RESIDUE, RECORDED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER: the judge ROSTER is not declared anywhere. `installed_judges_find_nothing` names, in its ACTUAL, which judges FIRED — it cannot name which judges PASSED, because judge_* returns findings and not attendance. So for the judge half of this stage the record is still a complaint list, and it is one for the exact reason the ruling names: a silent judge and an absent judge read the same. This is measured, not assumed — read judge_* in this module. Closing it wants attendance emitted BY the judge and a roster the entry can compare its ACTUAL against — filed as ticket a-judge-declares-its-attendance, not left as prose. Until it lands, the falsifier clause above holds only over the SHAPE half of this stage's record.
state_and_history: state.json + history.json beside this charter, BORN AT THIS ADDRESS'S FIRST CROSSING. Until a ticket crosses here there is no journal, and that absence is this machine's ordinary resting state rather than a missing file — a component that has never sailed has no voyage to record. CORRECTED 2026-08-14 (ticket a-charter-may-not-assert-a-file-that-is-not-there): this sentence read 'Both were born at the carve-out', which was false twice over — the files were not there, and no journal has ever been born at a carve-out anywhere in the system. orient's arrived weeks after its own carve-out, at its first crossing, and that is the mechanism for all eight. The fix is the sentence and never the files: an empty state.json here would manufacture a record of a voyage that did not happen (Law 7). The voyages that BUILT this stage before the carve-out are in the chart machine's history, which stays whole with the skill — a record of truth is never split.
gates: THE STAGE'S OWN INSPECTOR AND ITS OWN GATE, at this address (ruling 2026-08-13 every-machine-carries-its-own-inspector-and-gate). ``inspect_constrain`` returns a PROOF RECORD — one entry per check that ran, EXPECTED beside ACTUAL, passes included — and ``validate_constrain`` is the == compare over it, per entry, with no oracle anywhere near it. The shared half of the record comes from cairn/tools/chain's ``common_shape_record`` so the eight doors cannot drift apart; the stage-specific half is written here. Refusals still name every shape lack at once (ticket chart-doors-refuse-in-one-pass), and they are DERIVED from the record's mismatches, so the gate and the sentence it prints cannot disagree about what failed. A CHECK THAT DID NOT RUN IS ABSENT, NOT PASSED: guarded checks make the record SHORTER, never cleaner.
falsifier: RED on any of: (1) this stage reading its input from anywhere but the previous stage's BERTHED packet; (2) a door that dribbles refusals instead of naming every lack in one pass; (3) a packet admitted whose provenance does not cover every authored field; (4) this module importing a sibling stage — the legs speak the grammar, never each other. (5) a check in this stage's inspector that PASSES SILENTLY — every check that ran appears in the record with its EXPECTED beside its ACTUAL, and a check that could not run is ABSENT rather than passed, so a check that stops running makes the record SHORTER and never cleaner; (6) a refusal sentence assembled from anywhere but the record's own mismatches — the gate and the sentence it prints cannot be allowed to disagree about what failed; (7) an oracle consulted anywhere on this path, at fire time or at sleep — `bin/cmd/determinism` must keep reading this component PURE DETERMINISTIC and REFUSES GATE. (8) A FIELD WEARING A PROVENANCE LABEL THE FLOOR CANNOT REPRODUCE. The stratum for ``constraints`` and ``unknowns`` is measured at the gate, never accepted from the sender, and a packet that declares one and gets it wrong is REFUSED rather than silently corrected — a silent overwrite leaves the sender believing it still labels its own work. RED equally if the ``floor`` label becomes UNREACHABLE: the ceiling legitimately adds constraints in kinds the floor cannot reach, and a rule that demoted the field for those would make the label a constant, which is not a measurement and would leave the dial blind to the compiling it exists to watch. (9) A REF THE FLOOR CANNOT GROUND THAT LEAVES NO TRACE — a ref that resolves to no component rides out as an unknown carrying WHY, because 'not a component' is four different findings (ambiguous name, path that does not exist, path under no component, roster and lookup disagreeing) wearing one sentence. (9) A CHECK CONSTRAINT WHOSE VERDICT DID NOT COME FROM A RUN — a named list wearing verdicts is the failure this half exists to replace, and its tooth plants a proof built to FAIL and requires the floor to say red. RED equally if the report cannot DISCRIMINATE: three instruments in three states must appear in three states, because a blanket verdict is a constant with a longer sentence. RED if the check-set is ENUMERATED anywhere — Akien's ruling on this node, 2026-08-14, that it must "keep learning, not to become fixed"; the tooth plants a proof file at a ref'd address and requires it to appear with no code change, and a hand-written list is the only thing that fails it. (10) A KIND THE FLOOR EMITS THAT ``FLOOR_KINDS`` DOES NOT DECLARE, or a kind declared there that the floor never emits. That tuple is a DECLARATION and deliberately not a derivation — deriving it from a firing would shrink the set exactly when a run reached no instruments — and the price of declaring is a tooth asserting equality in both directions. It is load-bearing beyond this module: probes ASK the floor for its kinds rather than spelling one, so a stale tuple silently moves the line they are drawn on.
horizon: re-read when the chain's stage list changes, or when this stage's tree stratum goes live against a real embed seam.
how_it_learns: the deposit-back: every ceiling assembly deposits its own answer into this nexus's tree, so the next similar request walks to a settled answer instead of re-deriving it (Law 1 as runtime). The dial (cairn/skills/chart/dial.py) is the instrument that says whether the floor+tree fraction is actually growing — a nexus that never compiles is a ceiling doing the floor's job forever. AND THE DIAL IS NOW HONEST ABOUT THIS STAGE, which it was not before 2026-08-14: 24 of the 41 berthed packets declared ``constraints: floor`` while the floor as it then stood produced zero charter constraints for that same input in 24 cases — the number the staircase is steered by was computed by the party being measured. The cause was a name-keyed lookup asked of path-shaped data: the floor tested each ref for membership in the component ROSTER, a set of bare names, while 266 of the 310 refs across the 45 orient berths are PATHS. It discarded 86% of its own input and emitted an empty constraint list, which is a legal list and redded nothing. AND THE CHECK HALF LEARNS WITHOUT THE TREE AT ALL, which is the one place in this stage where learning is not the deposit-back. The instruments it reports are read off the working tree at fire time, so a proof added anywhere near the work is reported the next time the floor fires and nothing here is edited. That is the whole reason the set is discovered rather than enumerated: an enumerated set learns only when a human remembers it exists.

filed_edges: PROVENANCE ON A MIXED LIST IS PER-FIELD, AND THE HONEST SHAPE IS PER-ITEM. ``constraints`` carries charter, ticket, law, ruling and memory kinds in one list (measured over 41 berths: 148 / 110 / 63 / 33 / 14), and one label has to stand for all of them. The rule settled here — the floor's items survive unchanged AND no other charter-kind constraint appears beside them — is a true statement about the floor's share, but it says nothing about where the other kinds came from. A per-item stratum would, and the dial's per-field counting is what would have to grow to read it. Not built: the dial is another component's, and this stage would be guessing at a shape it does not own.

THE FLOOR REACHES CHARTERS AND NOTHING ELSE. Laws, tickets, rulings and memory are constraints the ceiling supplies, and 206 of the 368 constraints on the live berths are in those kinds. ``laws_note`` has said since the carve-out that surfacing the Laws as parsed constraints waits for a checkable shape; that is still true, and it is now the largest single block of ceiling work this floor could in principle take over. Nothing is designed here — naming the size of it is the point.

A REF THAT NAMES A COMMONS TICKET OR A SKILL GROUNDS TO NOTHING, and 47 unknowns across the live berths are exactly that. It is honest — no charter bounds a commons ticket — but 'exists but sits under no component' is a different answer from 'names nothing on disk' (115 of them, all refs written before the 2026-08-13 rung move), and only the second is a stale pointer. The floor tells them apart in the WHY; nothing yet counts the second kind and asks whether those berths should be re-run.

CARRIAGE IS NOT CONSULTATION, AND ONLY CARRIAGE IS MEASURED. The node's aim is that a build stops looking these instruments up by hand; what the armed probe (probes/lookups_stop.py) can see is whether the discovered checks SURVIVE into the berthed packet. Empty packets falsify the aim outright, so the necessary half is watched; full packets leave the builder's behaviour unmeasured, and the builder is Claude, which is Law 10's standing exception. The instrument that would close the gap is ticket the-builds-tool-calls-are-evidence-about-the-chart, and it is not this component's to build.

THE RUN COST IS THIS FIRING'S OWN AND IS NOT YET BOUNDED BY ANYTHING. Measured at 2.87s over the nine instruments this chain's own refs reach, against a 4.5s hand extrapolation — same order, so the selection rule holds today. Nothing caps it: a request grounding to a component with fifty proofs would pay for fifty runs at stage 2. The cache is keyed by (path, source fingerprint) so a second ask inside one firing is free, which is what the door's provenance re-run needs and is NOT a bound on the first ask. Named at its measured size rather than pre-solved.

A CHECK CONSTRAINT COUNTS TOWARD THE DIAL'S FLOOR FRACTION AND NOBODY DECIDED THAT IT SHOULD. It is a floor-authored constraint, so mechanically it does; the dial belongs to another component and this stage would be guessing at a shape it does not own. Recorded here so a rising floor fraction on the dial is not read as the ceiling compiling when part of it is this build changing what gets counted.
